paper_summary: Epoxy (E-51/100-1B) syntactic foams filled with 30 vol% 3M hollow glass microspheres (K1, S35, S60HS) were reinforced with warp-knitted spacer fabrics (B1-B4) to form 3DSMRC ternary composites, and compared with neat syntactic foam (NSF) under quasi-static compression (2 mm/min, 8 mm thick samples). Suitable WKSF (B1, B2, B4) raised yield strength by ~7-10% and compressive modulus by ~15-21% relative to NSF at nearly the same density, while NSF showed a higher peak stress; thicker-walled S60HS microspheres gave the best compression performance. A COMSOL FE model reproduced CWS60-30-B1 within ~8%.

extraction_notes: Absolute yield strength and modulus for the 3DSMRC samples are only shown as bars in Fig. 3(b) and as percentage differences relative to NSF in the text, so they are left null (percentages recorded in microstructure_notes). NSF modulus (1.17 GPa -> 1170 MPa) and yield stress (9.72e7 Pa -> 97.2 MPa) taken from Table 5, which the paper states were obtained from the NSF compression test; the Table 5 density of 953 kg/m3 matches Table 4. Strain rate computed as 2 mm/min / 8 mm = 4.17e-3 1/s. Cure at room temperature (24 h) recorded as 25 C. Radius ratio from Table 3 used for particle_wall_thickness_ratio. Particle density in Table 3 is the manufacturer nominal density. FE simulation results (yield 7.5% lower, modulus 8.5% higher than experiment for CWS60-30-B1) not given as absolute numbers, so no model records were created.
